hook_text: A tiny drip fills a cup every 10 minutes. How much water is that in a day?
clip_script: Cape Town, a water-saving project. 1 litre is 1 000 millilitres. A quarter of a litre? 250 ml, one measuring cup. The dripping tap fills a 250 ml cup every 10 minutes. In an hour, 6 cups: 1 500 ml, that is 1 and 1/2 litres. In a day, 24 times that: 36 litres! Lwazi's bath uses 80 litres; a 2-minute shower uses 20. Save 60 litres. A 5 litre bottle? 5 000 ml, 20 glasses. Change to one unit, then solve.
visual_style: A drip falling into a cup, cups stacking up into buckets, then a bath and shower side by side.
mood: Thoughtful and determined, like a class on a mission to save water.
pacing: The drip question, the quarter-litre fact, then the big daily total.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and measure a dripping tap at home.
